diagnostics.message: :resource.helm_release.karpenter: explicit depends_on of :module.karpenter is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class: explicit depends_on of :module.eks is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class: explicit depends_on of :module.karpenter is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.null_resource.update_kubeconfig: explicit depends_on of :module.eks is redundant — already implied by attribute references

data.aws_ecrpublic_authorization_token.token explicitly depends on module.eks, but its dependency on time_sleep.wait_300_seconds already establishes that ordering because the sleep depends on module.eks.
data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster already depends transitively on module.eks through time_sleep.wait_300_seconds; the additional explicit module dependency duplicates that ordering.
data.aws_eks_cluster_auth.cluster already depends transitively on module.eks through time_sleep.wait_300_seconds; the additional explicit module dependency duplicates that ordering.

module.karpenter already waits for module.self_managed_node_group through its dependencies on aws_eks_addon.aws_ebs_csi_driver and aws_eks_addon.eks_pod_identity_agent, both of which depend on that node group.

helm_release.karpenter already references module.karpenter.service_account and module.karpenter.queue_name in its values, so its explicit dependency on module.karpenter duplicates an implicit dependency.
helm_release.karpenter already depends on data.aws_eks_cluster_auth.cluster through module.karpenter, which explicitly depends on that data source.
helm_release.karpenter already waits for null_resource.update_kubeconfig through module.karpenter -> null_resource.apply_tigera_operator -> null_resource.update_kubeconfig.
null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class already references module.eks security-group outputs in its triggers and manifest, making its explicit dependency on module.eks redundant.
null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class already references module.karpenter.node_iam_role_arn in its triggers and manifest; the explicit dependency on that module output duplicates this data dependency.

null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class already waits for null_resource.update_kubeconfig through its implicit dependency on module.karpenter, which depends on null_resource.apply_tigera_operator, which depends on update_kubeconfig.
null_resource.apply_node_pool already depends on helm_release.karpenter through null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class, which explicitly waits for the Helm release.
null_resource.apply_node_pool already depends on module.eks through null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class and that resource's references to module.eks outputs.

null_resource.apply_node_pool already waits for null_resource.update_kubeconfig through null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class -> module.karpenter -> null_resource.apply_tigera_operator -> null_resource.update_kubeconfig.
null_resource.delete_daemonset already waits for module.eks through null_resource.update_kubeconfig, whose command references module.eks.cluster_name.
null_resource.update_kubeconfig already references module.eks.cluster_name in its local-exec command, so its explicit depends_on on module.eks duplicates an implicit dependency.

null_resource.create_calico_installation enables Calico as the cluster CNI, but it can run concurrently with null_resource.delete_daemonset, which removes the existing aws-node CNI. Make the Calico Installation depend on delete_daemonset so replacement CNI reconciliation does not race removal of the old CNI. Their shared dependency on update_kubeconfig does not order these operations.

aws_eks_addon.aws_ebs_csi_driver waits for the node-group infrastructure but not null_resource.create_calico_installation. Because aws-node is being removed, the EBS CSI controller pods need the replacement Calico networking before they can become ready; add-on provisioning can otherwise race CNI installation and time out. Order this add-on after create_calico_installation, and ensure that the installation provisioner waits for Calico readiness rather than merely submitting the Installation object. This also orders the downstream Karpenter deployment after CNI installation.
